task: PDF vector recovery for all hydroacoustic sources (source-vector-extraction-2026-11-07)
tool: PyMuPDF 1.28.0; RapidOCR (rapidocr-onnxruntime 1.4.4) for tick labels drawn as glyph outlines; extractor module vecx.py in the parent folder
method: Vector panels: page.get_drawings() gives every path; panels are found from numeric tick-label rows and columns (text layer, or OCR of glyph outlines) anchored to the axis lines; each axis transform is a least-squares fit of label value against position (tick-mark positions where they lower the residual; linear or log10, whichever fits better); every vertex of every path inside the axes is written (border frame, tick and grid strokes on the border are dropped; Bezier control points are kept and marked); text words inside the axes are written as rows with item_type text; small closed paths also get a marker_centre row (bounding-box centre). Multipliers printed as glyph outlines (for example x10^6) were read from the rendered page and are stated in each header. Tables: page.find_tables() or a word/line dump of the text layer; no values typed by hand. Raster items: colour mask per pixel column, stated in the header.
acceptance: calibration_status ok when both axes have relative residual (max abs residual / label span) <= 3e-3; flagged up to 2e-2; failed above that
statement_status: re-run: every file in this folder was produced by code in this session; numbers in the note are read back from these files

header.source: Duncan and Dall'Osto 2023, JASA Express Letters, doi 10.1121/10.0022761 (article PDF: not retrieved — ask Pete); figure image held in the repository
header.content: Sound-speed section with seabed (dark fill) and deep-sound-channel axis (white dashed line) against distance from the hydrophones
header.time_span: model section (path for the 8 Mar 2014 case as drawn by the authors)
header.x_transform: distance_km = -1423.53*px_col + 7.3311 (least squares on 8 OCR-located tick labels 1000-8000)
header.resolution: 1423.53 km per pixel column; 554.69 m per pixel row
header.method: Raster: seabed = top of the dark-navy run (R<15, G<15, 100<B<160) that reaches the bottom of the plot, per pixel column; sound-channel axis = mean row of white pixels (min channel > 235) per column where the white run is under 8 px tall (dashes leave gaps, left empty). Tick-label centres located by OCR (RapidOCR) on the PNG; values not typed by hand.
header.caveat: The repository note for Fig. 3 of this paper states that the authors' MH370 path is the Curtin 301.6 deg HA01 bearing; the same may apply here (not checked).
